The blind review (family_a/review/blind-review.md) verified that the affirmative hold preserves the incumbent and that registered release effects simultaneous retirement and replacement. Fresh excerpt readings (family_a/review/necessity.md) verified the two-Source instrument-and-disposition routes and rejected the proposed shorter route. The order-only sibling preserves the key and ordinary context (family_a/review/matched-sources.json). The bank paperwork and administrative email provide incidental kinship and non-operative detail; the frequent name and later note favour the incumbent, while promoting the signed draft favours the successor. Retain the verified cut-off and order controls without generalising from one expressly coupled two-person office.

Interacting gaps remain unisolated, positional or token shortcuts can reproduce some graphs, and D does not complete individual fact-level deletion coverage. Admitted B verifies one origin and its forward, not a matched change in repetition or a priority rule for genuinely independent accounts. E revision 3 and W revision 2 extend the technical inventory but not admitted coverage. A genuine correction limited to an identified derivative record and reference time is different from independent disagreement or retraction by the original informant.

Admitted controls isolate release versus hold, one express amendment locator, and one order-only permutation. N and O add technical evidence about execution status and administrative progress. None of these establishes the effect of an authorised cure after a missed deadline or licenses substituting a later document date for the reference time of a correction.

C verifies recovery of a rich invariant graph, not a placement or workload effect. X and T provide technical but unadmitted cases for native incidental support and scope of completed inspection. Trust-specific authority during a custodian transition remains distinct from scope of inspection. A single intact moderate pack can test its own proof but cannot estimate effects of volume or an interaction.

External retrieval, OCR and physical recovery require a scope change. A readable file can stipulate a missing artifact or field and test the consequences for graph support, but cannot measure acquisition, practitioner outcomes or prevalence.

result.portfolio_summary: Count one development history per family, not per matched condition or review mask. A, B, C, D and F are the five formally admitted histories. The technical inventory is twelve: those five plus X, T, N revision 3, E revision 3, W revision 2, O revision 7 and L revision 9. X and T explicitly await human admission; the packet supplies no admission for the other five technical additions. E's earlier concordance-to-withholding pair remains diagnostic only after its documentary-realism return; revision 3's technical qualification does not reverse that decision. The seven technical additions cover incidental firsthand correspondence, a 25-Source custody handover, counterpart execution, conflicting parentage and office accounts, title-application progress with office fixed, and civil-record sighting limits. Neither hypothesis approval nor technical qualification counts toward the ten-admitted-family planning target. The separate pre-giant technical goal of nineteen is seven histories short on the supplied count. Ranked reserve: BV first, for an economical test of a late notice made effective by a separate authorised act; BW second, for an authentic correction that repairs historical proof without resetting the current roster; BX third, for trust-specific control of authoritative entries across a moderate records handover, conditional on a stronger realism gate. The three test different questions: whether a failed route can be cured, what time and proposition a correction speaks to, and which custodian's entry can take effect for each trust. They do not duplicate the registered intermediate or 65-Source large workload commitments. No paid extraction observations or sealed inputs are supplied, so no claim about model difficulty, workload effects or practice prevalence is warranted.

evidence_dependencies: Fresh readers verify exact references, named endpoints, the receiver's independently recorded date, the authority and its bounds, and the signed decision's actual effect. Attach each necessary passage from one verified sufficient route to the same edge.

Test the signed decision, notice, intake extract, and acknowledgement as singletons and in the strongest short combinations. Check whether the decision itself certifies eligible receipt or repeats the full named notice. Credit genuinely sufficient shorter proof rather than demanding redundant citations.

Separately delete each indispensable fact and its copies, then independently rederive the full key. Verify the affirmative receipt evidence of lateness and the bounded significance of the request and acknowledgement; absence of a decision in a diagnostic is not evidence of refusal.
design.expected_sensitivity_or_invariance: The intact graph includes the beneficiary. Positive proof joins the named notice, the applicable terms, eligible receipt and the authorised acceptance. The logged receipt establishes why the ordinary route failed; the staff acknowledgement establishes handling only. A mask that defeats the alternative route leaves current support unresolved if no sufficient route survives; it does not establish revocation or an alternative beneficiary.
genres_and_provenance: Verified governing extract from the trustees' executed file: identifies the trust, both routes and their timing, and an independently supported office.
Signed applicant notice retained as actually received: identifies the applicant, the named provision and its ordinary case reference; its date records signing, not delivery.
Dated intake extract retained by the receiving office: records actual receipt and the notice reference from its inbound records.

Applicant's native late-acceptance request retained as received: identifies the pending matter and gives the applicant's own account of the reason for the delay, without determining receipt or outcome.
Receiving office's native acknowledgement retained with the request: confirms the request is logged for consideration, not granted.
Signed trustee decision retained in governance papers: identifies the notice it expressly accepts and dates the authorised decision.
Dated adviser brief: fixes the review boundary and distinguishes matters for implementation from the relationship question.
design.intervention: Score one intact natural file. Use separate review-only diagnostics removing the qualifying decision, the fact linking it to the notice, and the relevant receipt or authorising-rule fact, including copies and derived restatements where necessary. Mask the staff acknowledgement separately. Do not edit an interdependent receipt or decision history into a scored sibling.
invariants: Fix the actual receipt, deadlines, decision chronology, exact endpoints and cut-off in the intact file.
The independently supported office retains sufficient proof under focal diagnostics.
negative_controls: The applicant's request and the staff acknowledgement do not cure lateness, independently or together.
Masking administrative acknowledgement alone preserves the graph and sufficient proof; unrelated office survives the focal diagnostics.
design.scenario: The adviser has the original notice trail and a separately retained disposition of the applicant's request. The file affirmatively shows that the ordinary route failed and that the permitted alternative was completed before the fixed review.
shortcut_heuristics: Test late-means-never, request-accepted, receipt-equals-effect, and newest-signed-paper rules.
Audit subject lines, headings, filename labels, quoted requests, timestamps and ordering for a supplied verdict or an overlooked independent operative route.
success_criteria: Two isolated whole-file readers independently reconstruct the exact graph. Fresh excerpt and diagnostic readers verify the ordinary-route failure, the sufficient cure proof, the actual legal-effect statement in the fictional file, and the invariant office.

Stop if an ordinary short record bypasses the original notice, if the cure requires outside law or retrospective inference, or if the proposed split between acknowledgement and decision cannot be justified by the retainer.

feasibility.authoring_and_review_effort: Estimated person-hours: authoring and chronology 8–12; isolated whole-file and fresh excerpt or removal review 9–13; adjudication and audit 6–9; owner 2–4. Assumes one application, two complete reads and at most one pre-lock revision.
feasibility.documentary_complexity: Nominal 7 natural Sources. The rules, notice, intake, applicant request, staff acknowledgement, trustee determination and briefing have distinct purposes in one decision cycle.
feasibility.infrastructure_reuse: Reuse A's dated-effect checks, exact passage attribution, and independent rederivation of diagnostic keys.
feasibility.ontology_compatibility: Use beneficiary_of and independently supported existing predicates. Receipt, lateness, requests, cure and commencement dates remain in evidence or the companion register. Do not score a negative relationship.
risks_and_limits: One intact file tests a particular express cure mechanism, not the effect of adding acceptance correspondence or a general rule about late notices.
One current cut-off does not measure whether extraction would correctly reconstruct the historical roster before cure.

assumptions: The fictional terms explicitly define eligible lateness, who may accept the notice, the outer bounds on receipt and decision, and prospective effect without further approval.
The applicant and receiving office have independently documented sending and receipt. Release of a routine acknowledgement is not the trustees' qualifying act.
Include any implementation minute or operative record ordinarily available at the first review after the decision. Do not omit it to preserve a longer proof.
grounding.documentary_situation: The instrument provides an ordinary receipt deadline and expressly permits a particular trustee decision to accept an eligible late notice prospectively within a further window. The applicant requests late acceptance and receives a staff acknowledgement. The trustees subsequently decide the request in a signed record identifying the original notice. The decision acts on that notice; it is not a fresh designation.
grounding.legal_workflow: Review a named provision after the trustees have dealt with a notice received after its ordinary deadline.
grounding.meeting_purpose: Identify whether an existing notice acquired effect through a separately authorised act by the review cut-off.
practitioner_unknowns: Would the trust naturally allow prospective acceptance of a late notice instead of asking for an entirely new designation?
Would a staff receipt acknowledgement and the separate signed decision both be retained and available at that review?

references.relevance: Supports retaining instruments and trustee decisions for administration, not the proposed notice process, grace window or power to accept a late notice.

grounding.retainer: Advise on current named relationships before the next trust administration cycle, distinguishing correspondence handling from the trustees' decision.

objective.coverage_gap: R moves the underlying event across a deadline and cannot diagnose an independently authorised cure when lateness is affirmatively established. J joins evidence of delivery to an instrument; it does not distinguish timely handling of a request from a separate operative decision to accept an already identified late notice.
objective.failure_mechanism: An extractor may discard the provision permanently because the notice arrived late, equate acknowledgement with acceptance, or treat the later decision as a free-standing designation and omit the notice it acts on.
objective.falsifiable_hypothesis: The intact file licenses the named beneficiary through a qualifying late notice and its authorised acceptance. Exact complete recovery with sufficient attachment disconfirms those predicted errors on this file. The intended mechanism is not verified if the notice was independently effective or the decision would make the same designation without it.

evidence_dependencies: Verify the corrected name, its exact entry and capacities, the original-based knowledge statement, its receipt before review, and the independently effective succession. Check which exact framing establishes each relationship and why it is current or historical.

Test the correction, earlier extract, succession and current extract individually and in plausible short subsets. In particular, distinguish a successor instrument's corroboration of an outgoing trustee's name from an independent attestation of who settled the trust. If the correction is a sufficient singleton for the settlor, credit it.

Audit copied corrections, corrected replacements, headers, search metadata supplied as text and summaries for competing sufficient routes. Independently rederive every diagnostic key instead of treating a removed correction as proof the erroneous entry was true.
design.expected_sensitivity_or_invariance: The repaired founding entry supports the settlor; the later operative act supports the successor. Exact negative evidence is the correction's explicit replacement of the earlier transcription and the succession's effective termination of the former office, not the correction's issue date or silence about the former office. No negative edge is emitted.
genres_and_provenance: Earlier verified derivative extract retained as issued: identifies the trust, founding party entry and its stated founding capacities; the original remains with the authorised custodian.
Native practitioner query retained on the handover file: identifies the discrepancy and requests a recheck, without claiming independent knowledge of the founding entry.
Custodian's signed correction retained with the issue record and supplied to the adviser: cites its direct reinspection, exact affected entry, corrected name and limited scope.
Executed succession instrument retained by the trustees: establishes the end of the earlier office and the effective successor; keep any names ordinarily stated in it.
Separately retained verified current provision extract: supplies an independent ordinary relationship for the same review.
Dated adviser brief: sets the cut-off and specifies the reconciliation task without listing answers.
design.intervention: Score one intact file. In review only, delete the corrected identification or its scope link with all copies, and separately mask the succession. Rederive each whole graph: removing scope or succession can change what is licensed in ways other than simple edge deletion. Do not score an artificially uncorrected sibling.
invariants: The original, actual succession, exact-name policy, file availability and cut-off remain fixed in the intact condition.
The independent ordinary relationship has a sufficient route outside both disputed records.
negative_controls: The native query proves that a discrepancy was raised, not which name was right. The earlier and corrected issue are not independent reports of constitution.
The independent current provision survives the focal diagnostics. A historical first-trustee description cannot substitute for current office proof.
design.scenario: A genuine name discrepancy causes a practitioner to request a recheck of the issued founding extract. The answer repairs a specified entry from the original, not the succession instrument or the current roster.
shortcut_heuristics: Test latest-issued-wins, disregard-all-historical-documents, union-of-versions, and misread-correction-as-new-appointment rules.
Check filenames, ordering and snippets for leaked current or superseded status; use reordering only in review.
success_criteria: Two isolated readers independently recover the full exact-name graph. Fresh readers verify the positive routes and the exact limits on both the superseded name and the former office.

Stop if real document retention does not justify both issued records, if an original or replacement normally available settles the intended join without the correction mechanism, or if the distinction depends on an external rule about legal effect.

feasibility.authoring_and_review_effort: Estimated person-hours: authoring and version chronology 7–11; isolated whole-file and fresh excerpt or removal review 8–12; adjudication and audit 5–8; owner 2–3. Assumes two complete reads and at most one pre-lock documentary revision.
feasibility.documentary_complexity: Nominal 6 natural Sources. Two archive issues, the query, the separate succession record, the independent provision and the briefing serve distinct purposes.
feasibility.infrastructure_reuse: Reuse D's scope and fallback checks, B's origin tracing, A's office checks and exact same-edge proof review.
feasibility.ontology_compatibility: Use settlor_of, trustee_of and the independently licensed predicates at the cut-off. Earlier office, supersession and discrepancy handling remain in the companion register; do not add historical or negative edges.
risks_and_limits: A naturally explicit correction may be easy to interpret. The contribution is the distinction between repaired evidence and an operative change, not an estimate of correction difficulty.
Do not manufacture ambiguity by withholding a clean replacement or an independently dispositive succession recital.

assumptions: The supplied materials expressly distinguish a corrected transcription from an amendment to the original. They establish the custodian's recheck, the exact reference and reach of the correction, and the independently effective succession.
The founding record supports the settlor relationship without depending on continued office. The supplied correction provides the original-based evidence; readers need not inspect the original.

The earlier issued extract is retained because the practice must account for what it received and queried. Include any ordinarily supplied clean replacement and assess whether it bypasses the intended proof.
grounding.documentary_situation: A certified derivative extract mis-transcribes the name in a founding party entry that identifies the settlor and first trustee. After a practitioner query, an authorised custodian directly rechecks the unchanged original and issues a dated correction limited to that entry. A separately executed succession instrument establishes a later office change. The correction reaches the adviser after that change.
grounding.legal_workflow: Reconcile a retained founding extract with the documented succession before completing a trust records handover.
grounding.meeting_purpose: Resolve a transcription discrepancy while keeping the founding identification and the current trustee roster separate.
practitioner_unknowns: Would the custodian issue and retain an item-level correction alongside the earlier extract rather than only issue a complete replacement?
Would the succession instrument ordinarily repeat the outgoing party's founding capacity, independently settling the very discrepancy under review?

grounding.retainer: Verify the identity recorded at constitution and the separately established present office, without treating an archive correction as a new trust act.

objective.coverage_gap: I changes the record basis of a certified extract, not what an authentic correction does to an earlier transcription of the same original. R distinguishes event and report dates without testing selective reliance on a repaired derivative record. Unlike a source's self-correction of its own substantive account, the underlying founding act does not change: the later issue repairs its representation, while a distinct operative succession changes only current office.
objective.failure_mechanism: An extractor may discard the correction as stale, retain the superseded misidentification, or rank the latest-issued corrected extract above the succession and reinstate the first trustee.
objective.falsifiable_hypothesis: The intact file supports the corrected settlor identification and the separately proved current trustee, not a current trustee edge based on the founding role. Exact recovery and sufficient separate attachments disconfirm those errors. If ordinary records already prove the repaired founding identification without the correction, the intended dependence is not demonstrated.

proposals.title: A corrected founding record does not reset the current roster

evidence_dependencies: Fresh readers verify trust and provision identifiers, exact named approval, entry reference and date, the contractual trigger for live control, and the trust-level acceptance or expressly continuing control. Verify separately the scoped positive evidence of pending work and why legacy recording is not operative.

Test both posting extracts, each approval, protocol and log, the exception report and snapshot as singletons and in the strongest plausible subsets. Check particularly for an authorised keeper's independent confirmation of a current entry in the acceptance or exception records. Credit any genuinely sufficient route; do not enforce an unnecessary protocol citation.

Remove each necessary authority, linkage, posting or operative-rule fact with its copies, and independently rederive each full key. Audit native replies, shadow exports, headings and summaries for shorter or adverse routes and report what survives. A missing acceptance record does not by itself establish continuing predecessor control.
design.expected_sensitivity_or_invariance: The positive edge attaches to the trust for which the predecessor still had live-entry authority when it posted the approved person. For the other trust, the accepted transfer and the successor's scoped pending finding establish why the predecessor's recorded entry does not supply the operative step. No edge is added from administrative bookkeeping; no conclusion about later completion follows.
genres_and_provenance: Two verified governing extracts, one retained by each trust: identify the trusts, give live entry its effect, and establish independently supported ordinary relationships.
Two signed approval decisions, one retained on each governance file: identify the respective named addition without certifying posting.
Two dated predecessor posting extracts, one retained for each trust's records or migration reconciliation: identify the relevant entry, time and decision reference from the predecessor's own logs.
Agreed transfer protocol retained by both service offices: records the allocation of the live-entry function and the trust-level acceptance process.

Dated acceptance log retained by the receiving team and signed off for the handover: records accepted live control for one trust and explicitly identifies the other trust as still with the predecessor at the review.

Successor's dated exception reconciliation retained from its own live records: identifies the corresponding transferred-trust item as pending, within the reconciliation's stated coverage, without turning the predecessor entry into an effective posting.
Dated reporting snapshot downloaded and retained by the authorised administrator for checking reported particulars: gives reporting context, not an independent account of entry.
Native handover query retained by the adviser and service offices: seeks disposition of the outstanding processing item without attesting to its effect.
Dated adviser brief: identifies the record-keeping and reporting work and fixes the cut-off without stating the roster.
design.intervention: Score one unchanged natural file. In review only, remove the trust-specific transfer or continuing-control fact, the relevant live-entry and decision linkage, and the rule giving entry effect in separate diagnostics; remove dependent copies when testing facts. Mask the reporting snapshot and handover query separately. Do not fabricate a matched cutover edit that would put the independent logs out of alignment.
invariants: The two exact trust endpoints, valid trustee approvals, actual service chronology and one review cut-off are fixed.
Both trusts' unrelated relationships retain sufficient evidence independently of the focal postings and reporting reconciliation.
negative_controls: Approval and a predecessor record are present for both trusts. A blanket acceptance or rejection of either genre fails in at least one file.
The successor's pending finding is limited to its own records and cut-off. Removing reporting-only material preserves the graph, and the independently supported relationships on both trusts remain.
design.scenario: A single practice checks two continuing trust files as part of one service handover and reporting reconciliation. Exact trust identities are already established. The question is which office can make an effective entry for each file, not which file contains the right name.
shortcut_heuristics: Test one-cutover-for-all, newest-custodian, any-posting, approval-as-effect, and reporting-as-roster rules.
Check parallel row position, trust order, filename cues, duplicate origins and wrappers. A label may locate a record but cannot establish the scope of delegated authority.
success_criteria: Before authoring, justify each Source by its creator, distinct record-keeping or reconciliation purpose, custody and availability at the review. Two isolated readers then reconstruct the full exact-name graph from every Source, and fresh readers verify sufficient proof and independently rederived diagnostics.

Stop if the predecessor's post-transfer records have no real reconciliation purpose, if a normal current roster makes the scope distinction dispensable, if the cutover conflicts with either accounting trail, or if the moderate inventory would require padding. Do not substitute section-level keys for whole-file review.

feasibility.authoring_and_review_effort: Estimated person-hours: authoring and cross-file integration 16–24; blind whole-file and fresh excerpt or removal review 14–21; adjudication and audit 10–16; owner realism and readiness review 4–7. Assumes one staged handover, two complete independent reads and at most one pre-lock revision.
feasibility.documentary_complexity: Nominal 12 natural Sources. Six trust-specific governance and posting records, two transfer-control records, and four receiving, reporting, correspondence and briefing records support one records handover and reporting review.
feasibility.infrastructure_reuse: Reuse C's exact trust and invariant-graph checks, A's operative-date checks, and T-style custody and intact full-file review without changing the scorer.
feasibility.ontology_compatibility: Use exact Person and Trust endpoints and beneficiary_of with independently supported existing predicates. Custodians, system permissions, handover milestones and open implementation are evidence or register entries, not scored nodes or predicates.
risks_and_limits: A natural split in custody does not by itself establish that posting is operative. Reject the design unless the supplied terms establish that mechanism directly.
The two trusts within this one file do not constitute independent histories or a matched estimate of a cutover effect. Document breadth is descriptive.

assumptions: Each fictional instrument makes entry by the designated keeper under the agreed handover process the final operative step. The custodian records an already approved decision and has no discretion to select beneficiaries.

Transfer is expressly trust-specific and takes effect upon documented acceptance, not mere dispatch, service access or administrative activity. Continued predecessor entries have a normal reconciliation purpose after cutover and do not purport to be live entries for the transferred trust.

Record-keeping and checking reported particulars justify the inventory. The nominal count is a planning assumption for this retainer, not an estimate of usual practice. Use only fictional parties and locally scoped records.
grounding.documentary_situation: The governing terms make authorised live-register entry the final step for each trustee-approved named addition. The same predecessor keeps both operational and migration records while the two trusts change custody on different dates. One trust has transferred live control; the other remains with the predecessor. The predecessor records both approved names, but its records establish a live entry only for the trust still under its control. The successor independently tracks the other trust's pending entry.
grounding.legal_workflow: Reconcile the operative registers and reporting records of two continuing trusts during a staged change of records custodian.
grounding.meeting_purpose: Separate trustee approval, migration bookkeeping, authoritative entry and administrative reporting at a single review cut-off.
practitioner_unknowns: Would the same records service naturally phase these trusts separately while maintaining a non-operative migration ledger for the first?

Would trustee approvals, actual posting records, acceptance milestones and the successor's exception report be separately retained and ordinarily supplied at this review? Would an already available verified live roster settle the question by itself?

objective.coverage_gap: I contrasts two underlying record types at fixed issue status; it does not ask whether the same keeper's recording capacity has transferred for only one of two already resolved trusts. T bounds what was inspected, not who could make an operative entry. AR tests the authority of a decision-maker before deferred effect; here both trustee approvals are valid, and the separately delegated recording function changes by trust.
objective.failure_mechanism: An extractor may assume the predecessor retains authority everywhere, assume it lost authority everywhere, promote both approvals or migration entries, or cite a reporting snapshot for a correctly identified relationship.
objective.falsifiable_hypothesis: On the intact file both approvals remain valid, but the current graph includes only the addition with an authorised live entry, while unrelated relationships on both trusts remain. Exact recovery and sufficient same-edge attachment disconfirm the predicted errors. If trust-specific transfer is dispensable to distinguishing the entries, the intended authority mechanism is not verified.

stopping_criteria: Before activation, verify that the proposal tests its stated difference from the strongest older design. Defer if the recordkeeping, participant knowledge or timing is contrived, if a normally available controlling record must be suppressed, or if the same distinction has already been verified.

Require two isolated, independent reconstructions from the complete supplied file, fresh exact-excerpt and diagnostic reading, and a bidirectional audit from every edge to its evidence and from every apparent assertion to its treatment. Adjudicate before locking; reread any revision that changes support.

Credit every verified sufficient route, including singletons. Distinguish a necessary component of one route from necessity for the edge, remove all copies when deleting a fact, and independently reconstruct every diagnostic graph. Never treat review masks as scored conditions.

Stop if the intended outcome needs outside law, external retrieval, OCR, a negative predicate, an unscored entity type or a scorer change. Record unresolved propositions and explicitly supported limits separately from the graph.

Keep admission, technical qualification and reserve planning separate. Do not commission intermediate, large, giant, excluded or held-out work through this reserve; preserve all admitted hypotheses, keys and scores.
